relations.evidence_quote: The relevant Union institutions and the Member States shall take the necessary measures at Union and national level, respectively, to enable the collective achievement of the climate-neutrality objective set out in paragraph 1, taking into account the importance of promoting both fairness and solidarity among Member States and cost-effectiveness in achieving this objective.

R.label: European Parliament and Council (Union legislature, acting through this Regulation)

action: establishing a binding Union-wide climate-neutrality objective for 2050
setting a binding intermediate 2030 net emission-reduction target
object: Union-wide greenhouse gas emissions and removals regulated in Union law
relations.coder_note: [reviewer_attention: routine] Foundational duty-creating provision; both Member States and 'relevant Union institutions' are addressees of the obligation, with the Regulation itself functioning as R. No third actor performs a function integrated into this specific target-setting act; the Advisory Board's role in the later Article 4(3)-(5) 2040-target proposal process is analysed separately (see uncertainty log, U1) as legislative-drafting assistance to the Commission's own proposal, not target-directed intermediation.

relations.evidence_quote: Member States shall adopt and implement national adaptation strategies and plans, taking into consideration the Union strategy on adaptation to climate change referred to in paragraph 2 of this Article and based on robust climate change and vulnerability analyses, progress assessments and indicators, and guided by the best available and most recent scientific evidence.
action: adopting a Union strategy on adaptation to climate change
requiring Member States to adopt consistent national adaptation strategies and plans
object: adaptive capacity, resilience and vulnerability to climate change
relations.coder_note: [reviewer_attention: routine] Direct standard-setting relation: the Commission's Union strategy functions as a template Member States must take into consideration when adopting national strategies. Civil-society consultation on adaptation shortcomings (Article 5(3)) and the cross-reference to biennial reporting under Regulation (EU) 2018/1999 (Article 5(4)) are procedural details of the same episode, not separate intermediary functions (see uncertainty log, U10).

relations.evidence_quote: The EEA shall assist the Commission in the preparation of the assessments referred to in Articles 6 and 7, in accordance with its annual work programme.

I.label: European Scientific Advisory Board on Climate Change (Advisory Board)

action: assessing collective progress and consistency of measures with the climate-neutrality and adaptation objectives
issuing recommendations to individual Member States
object: Member States' national measures and collective progress towards the climate-neutrality and adaptation objectives
mediating_function: providing scientific and technical reports that the Commission must base its assessments on
assisting the Commission in preparing the assessments

distinction.note: The EEA and the Advisory Board are legally distinct bodies from the Commission; the Advisory Board's independence is expressly guaranteed (Article 12 inserting Article 10a(4) into Regulation (EC) No 401/2009: members 'give their positions completely independently of the Member States and the Union institutions').

function.note: Article 8(3)(b) names their reports as a required evidentiary basis for the Commission's assessments; Article 8(4) assigns the EEA an assistance function; Article 3(2) enumerates the Advisory Board's tasks in detail.

regulatory_integration.note: Article 8(3) uses mandatory language ('shall base its assessments... on at least') tying these reports to the Article 6/7 assessment of Member States' progress and national measures, which can result in individualised recommendations under Article 7(2) -- not merely supporting the Commission's own separate rule-making process (contrast the Advisory Board's Article 4 target-setting role, treated separately in the uncertainty log, U1).

evidence.note: Anchored in operative text, Article 8(3)-(4); Recital 37 reinforces but is not the sole support.

counterfactual.note: Article 8(3)'s mandatory 'at least' language means removing these reports/assistance would remove a legally required evidentiary input to the Article 6/7 assessment of Member States, not merely an optional convenience.

relations.coder_note: [reviewer_attention: conceptual_boundary] The Commission's Joint Research Centre (JRC), also named in Article 8(3)(b), is excluded from I because it fails the distinctness test: it is the Commission's own in-house research service, not a separate legal actor (see uncertainty log, U2). The EEA's Article 8(4) 'assist in preparation' clause is textually thinner than the Advisory Board's enumerated Article 3(2) tasks; whether it independently satisfies regulatory integration or is merely internal/clerical support to the Commission's own document is a documented point of interpretive tension (see uncertainty log, U3). This coding treats it as intermediation because it is explicitly cross-referenced to the same Article 6/7 assessment of Member States as the reporting function.

relations.evidence_quote: The Commission shall engage with sectors of the economy within the Union that choose to prepare indicative voluntary roadmaps towards achieving the climate-neutrality objective set out in Article 2(1). The Commission shall monitor the development of such roadmaps.

T.label: sectors of the economy (undertakings choosing to prepare voluntary roadmaps)

action: engaging with and monitoring the development of voluntary sectoral roadmaps
object: indicative voluntary roadmaps towards the climate-neutrality objective
relations.coder_note: [reviewer_attention: conceptual_boundary] Genuinely ambiguous whether 'sectors of the economy' choosing a wholly voluntary process constitutes a regulated target in the RIT sense, or whether this is facilitative soft-law engagement outside the scope of a regulatory relationship. No third actor is involved; the uncertainty concerns T's status, not intermediation.

relations.evidence_quote: The Commission shall engage with all parts of society to enable and empower them to take action towards a just and socially fair transition to a climate-neutral and climate-resilient society.
action: engaging with society for exchange of best practice
object: public participation and awareness on climate action
relations.coder_note: [reviewer_attention: routine] No actor-specific regulatory relationship: 'all parts of society', social partners, academia, the business community, citizens and civil society are named as participants in an open engagement process, not as a regulated target or an intermediary performing a defined function. The European Climate Pact (Article 9(2)) is an instrument/initiative, not an actor.

relations.evidence_quote: The Commission shall assess the consistency of any draft measure or legislative proposal, including budgetary proposals, with the climate-neutrality objective set out in Article 2(1) and the Union 2030 and 2040 climate targets before adoption, and include that assessment in any impact assessment accompanying these measures or proposals, and make the result of that assessment publicly available at the time of adoption.
action: self-assessing consistency of its own draft measures and legislative proposals
object: the Commission's own draft measures and legislative proposals
relations.coder_note: [reviewer_attention: routine] The Commission assesses its own forthcoming proposals for internal consistency with the climate-neutrality objective; the 'object' (draft measures) is not an actor, so no external target is regulated and this does not support a codable R-T relation.

uncertainties.evidence_quote: The projected indicative Union greenhouse gas budget shall be based on the best available science, take into account the advice of the Advisory Board as well as, where adopted, the relevant Union legislation implementing the Union 2030 climate target.
candidate_actors: European Scientific Advisory Board on Climate Change (Advisory Board)
uncertainties.reasoning: Assisting the Commission prepare its own legislative proposal for a new (2040) target is rule-making assistance, not mediation toward a target's conduct: at this stage no target's compliance is yet being regulated. The same actor occupies a genuine intermediary role in REL_C01_003's assessment mechanism -- illustrating that RIT roles are relational, not fixed to the actor.

uncertainties.evidence_quote: reports of the EEA, the Advisory Board and the Commission’s Joint Research Centre
uncertainties.reasoning: The JRC is textually 'the Commission's Joint Research Centre' -- an in-house Commission department, not a separate legal actor. Fails the distinctness threshold regardless of its functional contribution.

uncertainties.evidence_quote: The EEA shall assist the Commission in the preparation of the assessments referred to in Articles 6 and 7, in accordance with its annual work programme.
uncertainties.reasoning: Tension between reading this clause as integrated into the same Article 6/7 assessment mechanism as the Article 8(3)(b) reporting function (this coding's view, folded into REL_C01_003), or as merely internal/clerical support to the Commission's own document preparation, too thinly specified to independently satisfy regulatory integration. Recorded transparently rather than silently resolved.

uncertainties.evidence_quote: each Member State is invited to establish a national climate advisory body, responsible for providing expert scientific advice on climate policy to the relevant national authorities as prescribed by the Member State concerned. Where a Member State decides to establish such an advisory body, it shall inform the EEA thereof.
uncertainties.reasoning: Voluntary ('invited'), Member-State-internal arrangement; the notification duty to the EEA has no specified regulatory consequence within this Regulation. An EU-level R-T structure is not responsibly reconstructable from this provision alone.

uncertainties.evidence_quote: The European Council, in its conclusions of 12 December 2019, has agreed on the objective of achieving a climate-neutral Union by 2050, in line with the objectives of the Paris Agreement
uncertainties.reasoning: Prominent recital-only actor (repeated political endorsement of targets across five recitals) with zero mention or assigned function anywhere in the operative provisions (Articles 1-14). A clear case of the operative/recital evidentiary distinction: recital salience does not license a positive relation.

uncertainties.evidence_quote: The Commission therefore intends to propose a carbon border adjustment mechanism for selected sectors, to reduce such risks in a way which is compatible with the rules of the World Trade Organization.
uncertainties.reasoning: Forward-looking policy announcement with no operative implementation within this Act (the mechanism itself is a separate, later Regulation).

uncertainties.evidence_quote: the Commission has committed itself to developing a regulatory framework for certification of carbon removals based on robust and transparent carbon accounting to monitor and verify the authenticity of carbon removals
uncertainties.reasoning: Announced future policy commitment; no operative certification mechanism is established anywhere in the operative provisions of this Act.

uncertainties.location: Article 12 (inserting Article 10a and amending Article 11(5) of Regulation (EC) No 401/2009)
uncertainties.evidence_quote: The Advisory Board shall complement the work of the Agency while acting independently in discharging its tasks.
uncertainties.reasoning: Administrative/organisational hosting arrangement (appointment of Advisory Board members by the EEA's Management Board, shared budget, consultation on the Advisory Board's own work programme) rather than a supervisory regulatory relationship over a target. The Advisory Board's explicitly guaranteed independence supports, rather than undermines, its status as a genuinely distinct actor for REL_C01_003.

uncertainties.evidence_quote: The Commission, assisted by the Energy Union Committee referred to in point (b) of Article 44(1), shall adopt implementing acts to set out the structure, format, technical details and process for the information referred to in paragraphs 1 and 2 of this Article, including a methodology for the reporting on the phasing out of energy subsidies, in particular for fossil fuels, pursuant to point (d) of Article 25.
uncertainties.reasoning: A comitology committee composed of Member State representatives is more plausibly read as a Member-State oversight/co-regulation mechanism over the Commission's implementing power than as a target-directed intermediary. Its composition and voting procedure are defined in instruments (the comitology framework, Regulation (EU) 2018/1999) not reproduced in this corpus.

uncertainties.evidence_quote: identify shortcomings in this regard in consultation with civil society
uncertainties.reasoning: Open participatory consultation without an institutionally assigned function distinguishable from general stakeholder engagement; textbook external influence rather than intermediation.
